shorts.description:
Level 1 salesmen focus on getting better at sales. 

Level 2 salesmen focus on getting better people to sell to. 

Level 3 salesmen focus on getting better things to sell.

Level 4 salesmen don’t sell anything at all and simply make it easy for people to buy.

If you’re new to my channel, my name is Alex Hormozi. I’m the founder and managing partner of Acquisition.com. It’s a family office, which is just a formal way of saying we invest our own money into companies. Our 10 portfolio companies bring in over $250,000,000+ per year. Our ownership stake varies between 20% and 100% of them. Given this is a YT channel, and anyone can claim anything, I’ll give you some stuff you can google to verify below.

How I got here…

21: Graduated Vanderbilt in 3 years Magna Cum Laude, and took a fancy consulting job.
23 yrs old: Left my fancy consulting job to start a business (a gym).
24 yrs old: Opened 5 gym locations.
26 yrs old: Closed down 6th gym. Lost everything. 
26 yrs old: Got back to launching gyms (launched 33). Then, lost everything for a 2nd time. 
26 yrs old: In desperation, started licensing model as a hail mary. It worked. 
27 yrs old: "Gym Launch" does $3M profit the next 6 months. Then $17M profit next 12 months.
28 yrs old: Started Prestige Labs. $20M the first year.  
29 yrs old: Launched ALAN, a software company for agencies to work leads for customers. Scaled to $1.7mmo within 6 months. 
31 yrs old: Sold 75% of UseAlan to a strategic buyer in an all stock deal. 
31 yrs old: Sold 66% of Gym Launch & Prestige Labs at $46.2M valuation in all-cash deal to American Pacific Group. (you can google it)
31 yrs old: Started our family office Acquisition.com. We invest and scale companies using the $42M in distributions we had taken + the cash from the $46.2M exit.
32 yrs old: Started making free content showing how we grow companies to make real business education accessible to everyone (and) to attract business owners to invest or scale their businesses. 
34 yrs old: I became co-owner of https://Skool.com, which is a platform for people to build communities online, making a living doing what they love, with people like them.
36 yrs old: I did a $106M book launch selling 3.6M copies of my $100M Money Models book, in 72 hours, breaking the Guinness world record for the fastest selling non-fiction book of all time.

Today: Our portfolio now does $200M/yr between 10 companies. The largest doing $100M/yr the smallest doing $5M per year. Our ownership varies between 20% and 100% ownership of the companies. Many of them we invested in early and helped grow (which is how we make our money - not youtube videos).

To all the gladiators in the arena, we’re all in the middle of writing our own stories. The worse the monsters, the more epic the story.

You either get an epic outcome or an epic story. Both mean you win. 

Keep crushing. May your desires be greater than your obstacles. 

Never quit,

Alex

Imagine a marketer saying:
“There are no good customers out there.”

It’s kinda like an entrepreneur saying:
“There are no good employees out there.”

Getting talent takes 3 things:

1) Write a good ad (most suck)
2) Qualify the applicants (most don’t)
3) Pay well (most can’t)

shorts.description:
For every person that gives a reason why things are unfair to them compared to others and that’s why they haven’t seen success…

You’re right. 

Now what?

Just because it’s not your fault doesn’t mean it’s not your responsibility.
shorts.title: It's Not Your Fault, But It Is Your Problem

shorts.description:
Harsh reality:
Bad Operators add headcount.
Good Operators add process. 
Best Operators remove both.

Deletion is always the highest efficiency improvement.
shorts.title: When to Cut Underperforming Properties

shorts.description:
No one gets to the end of their life and says: I’m glad I did what everyone else wanted me to.

Sometimes your own approval needs to be enough.
shorts.title: Excuses Are Permission Slips for Mediocrity

shorts.description:
You’re not afraid of failing. 

You’re afraid of what other people will think of you if you fail.

But if you’re afraid of that, imagine what they think of you when you aren’t even trying.

Oh yea, they aren’t.
shorts.title: Do You Care More About Helping People or Being Judged?

shorts.description:
People say yes to bad opportunities for one reason: they’re in a rush.

Just because someone presents something doesn’t make it a gift.
shorts.title: Why Good People Walk Past Someone Who Needs Help

shorts.description:
The importance of betting big:

In entrepreneurship, you will lose more times than you win. So you just need to make sure that when you win, you win so big, it overshadows all your losses.

No one cares about small victories or defeats.
shorts.title: Your Business Works But Stopped Meaning Anything

shorts.description:
I need better words to say this but…the biggest motivator I’ve found is trying to meet the insanely high bar future me has for how hard I should try.

He never lets me off with a win.

I have to beat me, not them. 

Much, much, harder. 

But also 100% under my control.
shorts.title: The Secret to Life Is Stringing as Many Good Days in a Row as You Can

shorts.description:
If everyone saw learning skills as a real investment, more would do it. 

1) They go up in value 
2) They can’t be stolen 
3) Grow tax free
4) They compound each other 
5) Highest price to earnings ratio on the market. 

Double down on the one asset you hold forever - you.
shorts.title: Why Your Skills Are Worth Almost Nothing Right Now

shorts.description:
Beyond a certain level, no one works for you anymore. They just work with you.

Because the people at that level have 100 other options begging to have them.

So you’re not doing them a favor by giving them a career. They’re doing you a favor by building you a company.
shorts.title: How to Handle Team Pushback After Raising Prices

shorts.description:
3 types of business problems:
1) You don't have enough customers
2) You don't keep the customers you have
3) You don't make enough per customer

Figure out which one you're dealing with, put all your resources towards that, and ignore everything/everyone else.
shorts.title: You Step on the Tail, But You're Looking at the Mouth

shorts.description:
If you wanna win big, you’re not gonna have it all:

You’ll start earlier
End later
Work weekends
Skip beers w the boys
Miss a dance recital

Everything has a price.

You make a trade.

The thing you want less for the thing you want most.

Only you can pick which trade to make.
shorts.title: If You're Not Willing to Do This, You Don't Want It Enough

shorts.title: 8 Business Owners Compete For $100,000...

shorts.description: I didn’t know when I would become successful. But I knew I wouldn’t stop. That, I could commit to. That, I could control.
shorts.title: I Didn't Know I Was on the Right Path

shorts.description: Entrepreneurship is an unending process of trading your time for increasingly valuable activities. The myth is that you will get to a point where you no longer are needed, but if you continue to grow as your company does, you will become more valuable, not less.
shorts.title: If You Thought Entrepreneurship Was Easy Street, You'll Be Rudely Awakened

shorts.description: New entrepreneurs spend so much time trying to make their offer scalable, they forget to make it valuable.
shorts.title: Your Accountant Is Wrong (Here's What to Do Instead)

shorts.description:
The fastest path to $10M is often not the fastest path to $100m.

In this way, patience is strategy.
shorts.title: You're Shooting Yourself in the Foot Trying to Grow Too Fast

shorts.description:
Had a convo with a young founder who was “stuck” this morning. 

Here was my parting advice:

1) Change directions less. 
2) Stick with things long enough to see if it really worked. And if you don’t know yet. Then keep doing it. 
3) The more stable you are the more stable your team will be
4) You can attract and retain talent proportional to your personal growth
5) Your business is simple, don’t complicate it.
6) Focusing on getting better will make you bigger. But focusing on getting bigger will only spread you to thin.
7) Raise your people standards. 
8) Build from the customer backwards to money, not the other way around.
9) Remember you’re gonna die and it’s not gonna matter so don’t stress so much - you’ve already won.
shorts.title: 14 Years of Business Advice in 60 Seconds

shorts.description: “I’ve been getting copies by my competition, how would you react?”
shorts.title: A Billion Dollar Company Just Copied My Product

shorts.description:
Before saying you have ADD: put your phone in another room, turn off notifications, plug your ears, make a list, then work on the list.

You focus by removing everything but the work, not adding things.

Give yourself a chance before you say you have a disorder.
shorts.title: How to Stay Focused

shorts.description:
I am the biggest success story of every mentor/coach/vendor I’ve ever paid.

Here’s my “secret”:
Do everything they tell you to. 
To the tee. 
The first time. 
Take what works. 
Toss the rest.

You can learn something from everyone.
But only take in that which makes you stronger.
shorts.title: I Joined a Gym Mastermind Before I Owned a Gym

shorts.description:
A lot of entrepreneurship comes down to being able to look an existential threat in the eyes with equal parts dread and enthusiasm. 

And going from “this is gonna end us” to “we can turn this into a win” as fast as possible.
shorts.title: Choose Between Some Jobs Lost or All Jobs Lost

shorts.description:
If the words money and power bother you, you’ll never get them.

They’re neither good or bad.

They can build hospitals or fund terrorism.

But if you want to do big shit, you’re gonna need a lot of both.
shorts.title: Money and Power Can Save Countries. Peace Can Only Save Me.

shorts.description:
Who you sell to matters as much (or more than) the value you provide:

If you help a billionaire lose weight you can charge 100x more than gen pop. 

Because in a very real way, that more narrowly defined market values the solution at a higher dollar amount.
shorts.title: Same Sales Velocity, But LTV Is 5-10x Higher

shorts.description:
We’re all addicted to the same thing: reward. 

The only difference is what we get it from and where it leads us.
shorts.title: Give Someone a Label and They'll Change Their Own Behavior

shorts.description:
How to beat a bigger competitor: 
Talk to customers more than they do.

He who is closest to the customer wins.
shorts.title: You're Not Competing Against the Company, You're Competing Against Rep #7

shorts.description:
As silly as this sounds - almost no one does it:

If you’re trying to achieve something, the first step is having a way to measure progress.

And the more ways you measure, the more ways you can win.

So start there, then don’t stop winning.
shorts.title: How to Measure Customer Happiness

shorts.description:
Before saying you have ADD: put your phone in another room, turn off notifications, plug your ears, make a list, then work on the list.

You focus by removing everything but the work, not adding things.

Give yourself a chance before you say you have a disorder.
shorts.title: You Don't Have to Write, But You Can't Do Anything Else

31 yrs old: Started our family office Acquisition.com. We invest and scale companies using the $42M in distributions we had taken + the cash from the $46.2M exit.
32 yrs old: Started making free content showing how we grow companies to make real business education accessible to everyone (and) to attract business owners to invest or scale their businesses. 
34 yrs old: I became co-owner of https://Skool.com, which is a platform for people to build communities online, making a living doing what they love, with people like them.
36 yrs old: I did a $106M book launch selling 3.6M copies of my $100M Money Models book, in 72 hours, breaking the Guinness world record for the fastest selling non-fiction book of all time.

Today: Our portfolio now does $200M/yr between 10 companies. The largest doing $100M/yr the smallest doing $5M per year. Our ownership varies between 20% and 100% ownership of the companies. Many of them we invested in early and helped grow (which is how we make our money - not youtube videos).

To all the gladiators in the arena, we’re all in the middle of writing our own stories. The worse the monsters, the more epic the story.

You either get an epic outcome or an epic story. Both mean you win. 

Keep crushing. May your desires be greater than your obstacles. 

Never quit,

Alex

shorts.description:
Had a convo with a young founder who was “stuck” this morning. 

Here was my parting advice:

1) Change directions less. 
2) Stick with things long enough to see if it really worked. And if you don’t know yet. Then keep doing it. 
3) The more stable you are the more stable your team will be
4) You can attract and retain talent proportional to your personal growth
5) Your business is simple, don’t complicate it.
6) Focusing on getting better will make you bigger. But focusing on getting bigger will only spread you to thin.
7) Raise your people standards. 
8) Build from the customer backwards to money, not the other way around.
9) Remember you’re gonna die and it’s not gonna matter so don’t stress so much - you’ve already won.
shorts.title: Why Every New Opportunity Is the Woman in the Red Dress
